title: Bajaj Housing Finance Ltd - 544252 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Bajaj Housing Q1 FY27: record AUM addition of INR8,918 crore (AUM up 24% to INR1.496 lakh crore) and PAT up 23% to INR715 crore, but NIM fell 14 bps to 3.7%.
summary.overview: Disbursements rose 33% YoY to INR19,509 crore, a record quarter, and AUM grew 24% to INR1.496 lakh crore. PAT grew 23% YoY to INR715 crore, with ROA stable at 2.3% and ROE up to 12.5%. Net margin compressed 14 bps QoQ to 3.7% as portfolio yield fell, while cost of funds eased 7 bps to 7.2%. Q1 credit cost of 5 bps was flattered by a one-off assignment of about INR2,300 crore, and management guided FY27 NIM down 20-25 bps and credit cost at 10-15 bps.

segments.name: Home loans
segments.commentary: Growth improved to 20% YoY; 54.1% of AUM. GNPA moderated 1 bp QoQ to 34 bps. Balance-transfer-out pressure eased slightly in Q1, to be watched for one more quarter.

segments.name: Loan against property (LAP)
segments.commentary: Grew 22% YoY; 10.3% of AUM, down 50 bps QoQ in mix. GNPA rose to 62 bps from 46 bps on one-week account movement; management cites a 50-70 bps historical corridor.

segments.name: Lease rental discounting (LRD)
segments.commentary: Grew 41% YoY; 23.1% of AUM, up 70 bps QoQ in mix, the fastest-growing product.

segments.name: Developer finance (DF)
segments.commentary: Grew 19% YoY; 11.4% of AUM, down 10 bps QoQ. GNPA at 12 bps after one account moved from Stage 2 to Stage 3.

segments.name: Sambhav Housing (affordable and near-prime)
segments.commentary: Monthly disbursement run rate INR450-465 crore vs INR410-425 crore in Q4. Operational in 73 urban and 72 rural locations; target INR600 crore+ monthly in the next 9 months. About 65% of customers have bureau score above 750, and salaried mix is 68%.

guidance_outlook: NIM to moderate 20-25 bps in FY27 vs FY26 (FY26 3.9%); Q1 already down 14 bps, implying a further 6-10 bps decline across Q2 and Q3.
Cost of funds sideways in Q2 FY27 with a downward bias.
Opex to net income 19-20% for FY27, with possible upside; management says it will be broadly sideways vs FY26.
GNPA 30-35 bps and credit cost 10-15 bps for FY27; provision coverage 50-60% of GNPA.
Home loan industry growth assumed at 9-10.5% in FY27; company AUM growth guided in line with FY26 range (not explicitly quantified in call).
Leverage 5.8-6.3x, likely about 6.1x at year-end; ROA 2.1-2.3%; ROE guided at 12.5-13% for FY27.
Sambhav affordable ticket size INR17-18 lakh; overall Sambhav ticket size may drift down to INR26-27 lakh from INR28 lakh, with a downward bias of INR1-2 lakh by year-end.
capex_capacity: Sambhav Housing operational in 73 urban and 72 rural locations; geographic expansion into non-metro markets is a stated strategy.
Assignments run at 12-13% of AUM on a trend basis; Q1 included a large assignment of about INR2,300 crore, which released Stage 1 provisions.
Sambhav mix: 84:16 prime to Sambhav in home loans now, targeted at 80:20 by year-end FY27.
Borrowing mix: money market 52%, bank 38%, NHB refinance 10%; relationships with 18 banks.
demand_pricing: Management sees the industry demand as muted; growth may fall short of the 11-12% usually assumed. Home loan industry grew 9.4% in FY26. Management calls this a stabilisation phase as price momentum has paused.
Acquisition pricing in prime housing has been stable for some time; the company does not expect large-scale upward pricing moves and has not factored them in.
Portfolio attrition in prime home loans is running at a historical book at a higher yield than new business, which pushes yield lower in a stable rate environment.
Balance-transfer-out rate eased slightly in Q1 but remains under watch; the company is holding off on a more confident view until Q2 data.
Fee and commission income growth is linked to disbursement growth through insurance income and foreclosure, bounce and penal charges.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the 20-25 bps FY27 NIM compression, and is there any pricing relief or PLR hike possibility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the compression mainly to yield decline: high-yield book is running off while new business comes in at lower yields in a stable rate regime. Acquisition pricing has been stable, and no large-scale upward pricing move is assumed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q1 credit cost drop to 5 bps? Are there one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, two one-offs: a Q4 FY26 Stage 2 provision build that was not repeated, and a roughly INR2,300 crore assignment that released Stage 1 provisions. Management said to treat it as about 5 bps; the FY27 guide stays at 10-15 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NIM fall 13-14 bps when spreads were flat and cost of funds fell 7 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: The spread is computed on period-end portfolio yield versus average cost of funds, so it moved only 3-4 bps. The margin decline is from portfolio yield compression, which will continue through FY27 and offset the cost-of-funds benefit.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost of funds outlook for Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of funds is expected to be sideways in Q2 FY27 with a downward bias, helped by hedging, repayment of older high-cost borrowings and resets of some older borrowings to lower rates.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the LAP and DF Stage 2 to Stage 3 movement not raising provisions, and is there stress in LAP?
qa_highlights.answer: LAP provisions are formula-based on DPD, so roll-backs and roll-ins net off; the LAP movement was INR18 crore in total, not one account. DF provisioning was already held at 48-49% on the account. Management cited LAP GNPA in a 46-76 bps range over seven quarters and said there is no segment or geography concern.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Stage 1 provisions stay flat despite a INR7,500 crore rise in Stage 1 assets?
qa_highlights.answer: The annual January ECL recalibration lowered Stage 1 rates on most portfolios because credit performance was stronger, and the mix of new and attrited customers also shifted. Management said there is no simple pool-to-pool calculation.

risks_watch: NIM compression of 20-25 bps for FY27 with Q2-Q3 further declines of 6-10 bps; watch yield on new disbursements vs run-off.
Balance-transfer-out trend in home loans; a sustained easing would support AUM growth, but a reversal would pressure growth.
LAP GNPA at 62 bps, above the 50-70 bps corridor's midpoint trend; check whether the one-week account resolves.
Stage 1 provisioning appears light relative to the Stage 1 book; the credit cost guidance may need to rise to 10-15 bps as one-offs unwind.
Industry demand is muted and the company has said it is not assuming a rise in acquisition pricing; a rise in borrowing costs (MCLR, NCD) could pressure margins.
Opex to net income is expected to remain at 19-20%, so operating leverage is limited in FY27 as margins compress.
Sambhav ticket size and Tier 2/3 expansion may dilute average ticket size and yield; the affordable segment is ramping.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and asset quality, with the management assessment framed as cautious and assumption-based. Management was candid on margin pressure and deflected on pricing and demand questions with qualified language such as "we will watch for one more quarter."
